extracted.intended_audience: LTCH administrators, hospital finance officers, Medicare payment policy stakeholders, and public commenters on the FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed FY 2027 policy and calculation methodology for Long-Term Care Hospital (LTCH) Prospective Payment System items including COLA factors, CCR determination, high-cost outlier (HCO) payments, fixed-loss amounts, site-neutral payments, and IPPS-comparable DSH adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: COLA factors calculation using DOD OCOLAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the DOD OCOLAs as the data source to calculate COLA factors for Alaska and Hawaii; where locality areas must be combined (e.g., College, Eielson AFB, Fairbanks; Maui and Molokai), average the DOD OCOLAs for those locality areas to obtain the COLA factor for the OPM designated area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting with FY 2027, CMS proposes to no longer cap COLA factors at 25 percent (the prior OPM statutory cap) and is exercising discretionary authority to eliminate the 1.25 cap. CMS proposes to continue updating COLA factors at the same time the labor-related share of the IPPS market basket is updated for fiscal years after FY 2027. CMS solicits comments on the use of DOD OCOLAs, including how survey data specific to Service members (e.g., access to discounted commissary prices) may cause differential impacts, and on potential modifications such as a phase-in or transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCO payment trigger and payment share
rubrics_metrics.description: An HCO adjustment applies when the estimated cost of a case (calculated by multiplying the Medicare allowable covered charge by the hospital's overall CCR) exceeds a fixed-loss amount; the LTCH receives 80 percent of the difference between the estimated cost of the case and the applicable HCO threshold (the sum of the LTCH PPS payment for the case and the applicable fixed-loss amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This payment rule is applied for both LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases and site neutral payment rate cases, as applicable under the dual-rate structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-rate HCO targets and fixed-loss amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a bifurcated HCO policy under the dual-rate LTCH PPS: retain the historic 8-percent HCO target for LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases (resulting in a fixed-loss amount producing estimated HCO payments equal to 7.975 percent), and for site neutral payment rate cases adopt the IPPS operating HCO target (currently 5.1 percent) with the IPPS fixed-loss amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the bifurcated policy the fixed-loss amounts and targets differ by payment rate; CMS applies budget-neutrality adjustments where required (see site-neutral budget neutrality). References: §412.525 and §412.522.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and sourcing of overall CCRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute an LTCH's overall CCR based on the sum of LTCH operating and capital costs compared to total Medicare charges (operating and capital inpatient routine and ancillary charges) from the most recently settled or most recent tentatively settled cost report from the latest cost reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In certain instances CMS may use an alternative CCR such as a statewide average CCR, a CCR specified by CMS, or a CCR requested by the hospital. Other sources the MAC may consider include data from a different cost reporting period, the cost reporting period preceding LTCH status, or comparable LTCHs (same chain/region). See §412.525(a)(4)(iv) and §412.522(c)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH total CCR ceiling policy (3-SD rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An LTCH with a calculated CCR in excess of the LTCH total CCR ceiling (calculated as 3 standard deviations from the national geometric average CCR) is generally assigned the applicable statewide average CCR, because CCRs above the ceiling are presumed likely to be due to faulty data reporting or entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to determine the LTCH total CCR ceiling using best available IPPS total CCR data (December 2025 PSF) and proposes an LTCH total CCR ceiling of 1.354 for FY 2027. CMS will use best available data in the final rule and refers to the FY 2007 IPPS final rule methodology for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statewide average CCR determination and when MACs may use it
rubrics_metrics.description: Statewide average CCRs for LTCH PPS are determined similarly to the LTCH CCR ceiling methodology (based on total IPPS CCR data); a MAC may use a statewide average CCR when (1) a new LTCH has not submitted a first Medicare cost report, (2) an LTCH's calculated CCR exceeds the total CCR ceiling, or (3) data to calculate a CCR are not available (e.g., missing or faulty data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to use IPPS 'total CCR' data from the December 2025 PSF to set statewide average CCRs for urban and rural hospitals effective Oct 1, 2026–Sept 30, 2027 (Table 8C). CMS may use proxies (e.g., national averages) where trimmed CCR data are not available for a state's rural areas and will rely on best available data for the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation of HCO payments at settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: HCO payments are subject to reconciliation at settlement based on the CCR calculated from the cost report coinciding with the discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS refers readers to Medicare Claims Processing Manual sections 150.26–150.28 and to Change Request 7192 and Change Request 14233 (Transmittal 13428) for details and recent updates to outlier reconciliation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-loss amount setting for standard Federal payment rate cases (FY2027 proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fixed-loss amount is set so estimated aggregate HCO payments for LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases equal 99.6875 percent of 8 percent (i.e., 7.975 percent) of estimated aggregate LTCH PPS payments for those cases; for FY 2027 CMS proposes to maintain the FY 2026 fixed-loss amount of $78,936.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS departed from its historical methodology for FY 2027 because of uncertainty introduced by expanded reconciliation criteria and large recent charge inflation. Using a range of assumptions produced a wide fixed-loss range (~$67,000 to $109,000); CMS chose stability by keeping the FY 2026 level, intending to reassess once more representative data are available. References to statutory authority: section 123(a)(1) of BBRA and section 307(b)(1) of BIPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: CR14233 expanded outlier reconciliation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Change Request 14233 expands MAC identification criteria for referring cost reports to CMS: for cost reports beginning on/after Oct 1, 2025, identify instances where (1) actual CCR is plus or minus 20 percent or more from the CCR used during that period to make outlier payments, and (2) total outlier payments exceeded $500,000 (expanded from the original ±10 percentage points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS' analysis of FY 2023 cost reports found ~2% met original criteria vs ~24% meeting expanded criteria. Many cost reports subject to the expanded criteria reflected LTCH charge increases that far exceed costs, contributing to uncertainty in using recent data to estimate future outlier payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site neutral payment rate fixed-loss amount and HCO payments
rubrics_metrics.description: For site neutral payment rate cases, CMS proposes the fixed-loss amount equal to the IPPS fixed-loss amount for the fiscal year (proposed FY 2027 IPPS fixed-loss amount = $51,679). HCO payments for site neutral cases equal 80 percent of the difference between the estimated cost and the HCO threshold (site neutral payment rate + fixed-loss amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains the use of IPPS fixed-loss amounts for site neutral cases historically (FYs 2016–2025) because historical claims data were not fully subject to the site-neutral rate and because actuaries projected differences in costs/resource use; CMS retains this approach for FY 2027 due to limited post-PHE data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality adjustment for site neutral HCO payments
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure estimated site neutral HCO payments do not increase aggregate LTCH PPS payments, CMS applies a budget neutrality adjustment by reducing the site neutral payment rate amount by 5.1 percent (applying a multiplicative factor of 0.949) to account for estimated additional HCO payments payable to site neutral cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 5.1 percent reduction is applied to the site neutral payment rate under §412.522(c)(1)(i) for FY 2027. Consistent with current policy, the budget neutrality adjustment is not applied to the HCO portion of the site neutral payment rate amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPPS comparable/equivalent amount DSH payment adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating the 'IPPS comparable amount' (SSO) and 'IPPS equivalent amount' (site neutral), include a reduced Medicare DSH operating payment amount that reflects statutory changes from ACA section 3133 (separate empirically justified Medicare DSH payments and uncompensated care payments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to include an operating Medicare DSH payment amount equal to 73.75 percent of the amount that would have been paid prior to the ACA amendments (25% + (75% * 65.00%) = 73.75%). CMS will update the projected percentage annually consistent with uncompensated care payment determinations and use most recent data in the final rule where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of adjusted LTCH PPS Federal prospective payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate is adjusted for area wages by multiplying the labor-related share of the payment by the applicable LTCH PPS wage index and adding the nonlabor-related portion (adjusted for COLA, if applicable); multiply the adjusted rate by the MS-LTC-DRG relative weight to obtain the total adjusted Federal prospective payment for the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provides a numeric example: unadjusted standard Federal payment rate $52,177.04; proposed labor-related share 73.0%; proposed wage index 1.0107; nonlabor 27.0%; MS-LTC-DRG relative weight 0.9688; resulting adjusted payment $50,943.95. Tables with proposed wage index and relative weights (Tables 11, 12A–12B) are available on the CMS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'best available data' and proxy choices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will use the best available data (e.g., December 2025 Provider Specific File) to determine LTCH total CCR ceiling, statewide average CCRs, DSH percentages, and other rates; where data are missing or unreliable, CMS will use proxies (e.g., national averages) or previously established methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: using national average total CCR for Maryland proxies due to suspected PSF data inaccuracy; using national rural averages for certain states lacking trimmed CCR data. CMS plans to use updated data in the final rule if available and to reference prior final rule methodology (e.g., FY 2007 IPPS final rule).
